text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government MP injured in a car crash where a police chief and an organised crime boss died says he was the victim of a plot.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz says Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller's businessman husband Ozer is implicated in the murder of a casino owner.
- Head of the military gives assurances that Turkey will not be taken back to the dark Middle Ages by Islamists.
- Leftist leader Deniz Baykal says the organised crime gang exposed in a security scandal is still active and may seek revenge.
- Intelligence service report emphasises the need to disband state-paid militia force fighting Kurdish rebels in southeast.
- Plastic products producers worried by partial strike at Petkim oil refiner.
- Parties, except ruling Islamist Welfare Party, agree on a law limiting immunity rights of deputies.
- Council of State annuls Justice Ministry regulation which would enable women who wear the Islamic headscarve to work as lawyers.
